summary: Unusual IAM role approval chain triggered after clicking recruiting portal iframe
description:
Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 at ~08:14 UTC our identity monitoring alerted to a rapid sequence of IAM role approvals originating from an employee browser session after they interacted with an external recruiting portal embedded as an iframe. The approvals were non-standard (bypassed usual manager approval step via an automated OAuth/OIDC approval flow).

Impact: Temporary elevation for three internal service roles and creation of two ephemeral service-principals. No confirmed lateral movement at time of writing, but the approved roles allowed token minting and limited access to internal artifact storage. Potential exposure window: ~08:14–08:27 UTC.

Environment: Production (us-east), IdP: Okta SSO, internal auth gateway, proxy: corp-proxy-1. Affected user: contractor (non-engineering vendor) with corporate device.

Steps to reproduce (observed flow):
1) Employee clicks link to "Update candidate profile" on external recruiting portal (recruiting-portal.example[.]com).
2) Page contains an embedded iframe pointing at a third-party applicant viewer.
3) Iframe triggers a silent redirect to our IdP authorize endpoint with prompt=none omitted; browser displayed an approval popover that the user clicked (appeared as an inline consent).
4) IdP issued an authorization code; internal integration automatically exchanged it and called the IAM approval API, which (due to a relaxed service-to-service validation) created ephemeral approvals for role assumption.

Observed evidence / logs (high level):
- Okta events: multiple OIDC authorize events for user alice.jenkins@redwood.com (contractor) from referrer recruiting-portal.example.com at 2026-03-10T08:14:23Z.
- Auth gateway logs: Elevated session token minted by integration-service-broker (svc-broker-17) 2026-03-10T08:14:27Z.
- IAM audit: APPROVE_ROLE events for roles infra/deploy and ci/runner at 08:14:29Z, 08:14:31Z, 08:15:02Z. Approvals show actor = svc-broker-17 (service principal).
- Network: outbound connections to 52.149.84.22 (hosting provider for third party) at same timestamps. Geo: EU.
- No large data transfers observed to external endpoints in the window; internal artifact read-ops minimal.

Investigation summary:
- Hypothesis: Clickjacking or malicious iframe induced a consent/approval flow that our internal broker accepted. The broker's validation logic lacks strict referrer/origin checks for OIDC callbacks from external origins.
- Evidence supporting hypothesis: referrer headers and Okta redirect_uri mismatch warning present in Okta logs; broker accepted without additional allowlist checks.
- Scope: Three role approvals, two ephemeral service-principals created and used by a short-lived CI job. CI job pulled a small test artifact from private-storage but did not create outbound transfers.

Immediate actions taken (timeline):
- 2026-03-10 08:30 UTC: SRE (Liam Chen) revoked the three ephemeral role approvals and disabled svc-broker-17.
- 2026-03-10 08:35 UTC: Security (Aisha Malik) forced SSO session revocation for affected user and all active sessions for svc-broker-17.
- 2026-03-10 08:40 UTC: Proxy team blocked recruiting-portal.example[.]com at the corporate proxy and added domain to SIEM watchlist.
- 2026-03-10 09:05 UTC: Rotate keys for the two ephemeral service-principals and removed their tokens.
- 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC: Started forensic endpoint scan on contractor device (ENG-LENOVO-14).

Current status and risk:
- Risk of ongoing compromise appears low: no persistent credentials found, broker was disabled and tokens revoked.
- Potential for similar attacks remains until broker validation is hardened.

Required follow-ups (post-incident):
- Code change to broker to validate redirect_uri, require exact origin match and an allowlist for third-party integration. (Assigned: infra-auth team).
- Add behavioral alert for rapid ephemeral role approvals (>2 approvals per minute per actor).
- Full postmortem documenting timeline, root cause, and rollout plan.
- Communicate to vendor contractor onboarding teams about not clicking external iframes for SSO flows.

References: Slack #sec-ops thread link, Okta event ids and IAM audit ids attached in related_confluence_pages.
comments: 2026-03-10 08:33 - Liam Chen (SRE): Initial triage: revoked approvals (APPROVE_IDs 78522/78523/78524), disabled svc-broker-17. Blocking domain at proxy. Will follow up with endpoint scans.
2026-03-10 08:45 - Aisha Malik (Security): Forced SSO session revocation for affected user and any sessions issued via svc-broker-17. Notifying vendor manager to isolate contractor device.

2026-03-10 09:15 - Jenna Ortiz (Endpoint IR): Endpoint scan on ENG-LENOVO-14 returned 'suspicious browser extension' and one unknown background process; quarantined and collecting disk image. No signs of credential exfil reported so far.

2026-03-10 10:30 - Rahul Patel (IAM): Confirmed broker accepted redirect_uri variations; missing strict origin check. Preparing PR to add origin allowlist and require verification of client_id mapping.

2026-03-11 14:02 - Liam Chen (SRE): Temporary mitigation deployed: broker disabled in prod and replaced with a proxy that enforces redirect origin checks; added detection alert rule for >2 approvals/min by actor.
2026-03-12 09:00 - Aisha Malik (Security): No additional anomalous activity detected in 48 hours. Postmortem ticket created: INT-226489. Follow-up tasks assigned to infra-auth and hr/vendor-ops.
investigation_notes: Forensics: Disk image from contractor laptop included a browser extension 'FormHelper' (CRX ID: ejfhk1) not approved by IT; extension injects iframes into third-party forms. Static analysis of extension shows code paths that listen for 'click' events and simulate consent button clicks in embedded frames. Network captures correspond to 3rd-party hosting in EU; user agent strings match contractor's device. IAM logs indicate broker did not verify origin header on callback and accepted token exchange when client_id matched. No evidence of long-lived key theft. CI job logs: job 98321 authenticated using ephemeral creds and pulled a 12KB artifact; auth logs show no external uploads.
resolution: Mitigation completed: ephemeral approvals revoked, svc-broker-17 disabled and replaced with hardened proxy, affected tokens rotated, external domain blocked, endpoint quarantined. Detection rule and allowlist changes merged to staging. Full postmortem scheduled (INT-226489).  Remediation PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5216 (broker origin validation), github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/211 (detection rules).
notes_for_followup: 1) Harden broker validation and promote to prod; 2) run vendor device audits and update onboarding policy to block unapproved extensions; 3) re-run IAM audit for last 30 days to detect similar patterns; 4) add automated tests for redirect_uri/origin checks in CI.
